items.title: Carmen Caramanica interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, July 27, 2011
items.q: I had Raquel Welch’s gig, which was a show. It was world-class musicians, but we were playing a show.

ctx.x: Well I’ve heard other people — Herb Ellis said the same thing. He said you should be singing — be able to sing what you want to play I guess. But he apparently did the same thing, he would sing along. So did you eventually get burned out with the road and being away?

You know I did and I think a lot of it had to do with I kind of made a choice to become a career musician rather than a dedicated artist. And this is something that happens to a lot of people. If you’re lucky enough to play the kind of music professionally that you want to play to the exclusion of everything else, then you’re dedicated to your craft, you’re dedicated to your art, and you go where that takes you. But you’re happy doing what you’re doing and you’re not worried about well let’s see I have to support…

nights a week, two shows a night. You know you can burn out on that stuff because you’re not playing what you want to play anyway, and yet you’re doing it all over the country, all over the world, and you’re not home, and all the negatives take on more importance. So yeah, burn out happens. And you get to the point where you say I’d rather do something else, not necessarily rather do something other than music, but I’d rather not just keep doing this. And of course in Tony’s case he went from being very, very,…
